1	# Frontier AI Models Compared: Intelligence, Speed & Cost
     2	
     3	Based on independent analysis from Artificial Analysis (artificialanalysis.ai), this brief compares the leading frontier AI language models across three critical dimensions: intelligence, output speed, and pricing. All data reflects the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.0.
     4	
     5	## Intelligence Rankings
     6	
     7	The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index aggregates performance across 10 rigorous evaluations including GDPval-AA, τ²-Bench Telecom, Terminal-Bench Hard, SciCode, AA-LCR, AA-Omniscience, IFBench, Humanity's Last Exam, GPQA Diamond, and CritPt. Scores represent a holistic measure of model capability across coding, agentic tasks, knowledge, and reasoning.
     8	
     9	| Model | Intelligence Score |
    10	|---|---|
    11	| Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview | 57 |
    12	| GPT-5.4 (xhigh) | 57 |
    13	| Claude Opus 4.6 (max) | 53 |
    14	| Muse Spark | 52 |
    15	| Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max) | 52 |
    16	| GLM-5.1 | 51 |
    17	| Grok 4.20 0309 v2 | 49 |
    18	| Gemini 3 Flash | 46 |
    19	| DeepSeek V3.2 | 42 |
    20	| NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super | 36 |
    21	| gpt-oss-120B (high) | 33 |
    22	
    23	Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and OpenAI's GPT-5.4 share the top position at 57, while Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 follows closely at 53. A notable 24-point gap separates the top-scoring models from the budget-tier gpt-oss-120B.
    24	
    25	## Output Speed
    26	
    27	Output speed, measured in tokens generated per second, is critical for latency-sensitive applications. Interestingly, the fastest models are not the most intelligent.
    28	
    29	| Model | Output Speed (tokens/sec) |
    30	|---|---|
    31	| gpt-oss-120B (high) | 206 |
    32	| NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super | 193 |
    33	| Grok 4.20 0309 v2 | 162 |
    34	| Gemini 3 Flash | 149 |
    35	| Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview | 129 |
    36	| GPT-5.4 (xhigh) | 72 |
    37	| Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max) | 48 |
    38	| GLM-5.1 | 40 |
    39	| Claude Opus 4.6 (max) | 40 |
    40	| DeepSeek V3.2 | 31 |
    41	
    42	The budget-oriented gpt-oss-120B leads at 206 tokens/sec — nearly 7× faster than DeepSeek V3.2 at 31 tokens/sec. The top intelligence models (Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.4) sit in the mid-range for speed.
    43	
    44	## Pricing
    45	
    46	Pricing is expressed as USD per 1 million tokens (blended input/output). The cost spread across models is dramatic.
    47	
    48	| Model | Price (USD / 1M tokens) |
    49	|---|---|
    50	| gpt-oss-120B (high) | $0.30 |
    51	| DeepSeek V3.2 | $0.30 |
    52	| NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super | $0.40 |
    53	| Gemini 3 Flash | $1.10 |
    54	| GLM-5.1 | $2.10 |
    55	| Grok 4.20 0309 v2 | $3.00 |
    56	| Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview | $4.50 |
    57	| GPT-5.4 (xhigh) | $5.60 |
    58	| Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max) | $6.00 |
    59	| Claude Opus 4.6 (max) | $10.00 |
    60	
    61	The cheapest options (gpt-oss-120B and DeepSeek V3.2 at $0.30) cost 33× less than the most expensive (Claude Opus 4.6 at $10.00). Premium intelligence comes at a steep price premium.
    62	
    63	## Key Trade-Off Insights
    64	
    65	- **Best overall intelligence**: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and GPT-5.4 (tied at 57) but at mid-to-high cost ($4.50–$5.60).
    66	- **Best value**: gpt-oss-120B offers the fastest speed (206 tok/s) and lowest price ($0.30) but ranks last in intelligence (33).
    67	- **Balanced pick**: Gemini 3 Flash scores 46 in intelligence, 149 tok/s in speed, and costs just $1.10 — a strong middle ground.
    68	- **Premium tier**: Claude Opus 4.6 delivers 53 intelligence but is the slowest (40 tok/s) and most expensive ($10.00).
    69	
    70	## Methodology
    71	
    72	The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.0 incorporates 10 independent evaluations spanning coding, agentic tasks, scientific reasoning, knowledge accuracy, hallucination resistance, and instruction following. All measurements are conducted independently by Artificial Analysis using standardized conditions.

Trigger on requests like "visualize this," "make a deck," 9 "create a slide," "build an infographic," "show me a dashboard," "make this visual," 10 or any request to present information in a visual HTML format. 11 license: MIT 12 metadata: 13 author: careerhackeralex 14 version: 0.3.0 15 category: document-creation 16 tags: [visualization, html, slides, dashboard, infographic] 17 --- 18 19 # Visualize 20 21 Turn any idea, data, or content into a stunning single-file HTML visualization. 22 23 ## After Creating a File 24 25 **Always do BOTH of these after writing the HTML file:** 26 27 1. **Auto-open in browser:** Run `open .html` (macOS) or `xdg-open .html` (Linux) so the user sees it immediately 28 2. **Return the file path as a clickable URL:** Include `file://` in your response so the user can click to open it 29 30 Example response after creation: 31 ``` 32 Created your visualization! Opening in browser now... 33 📄 file:///Users/you/project/my-dashboard.html 34 ``` 35 36 ## Critical Requirements (NON-NEGOTIABLE) 37 38 ⚠️ **EVALUATION FAILURE GUARANTEED WITHOUT THESE 8 ELEMENTS** ⚠️ 39 40 **EVERY file MUST start from the skeleton template in [references/skeleton.md](references/skeleton.md) — copy the ENTIRE template, then add your content.** 41 42 1. **CSS Custom Properties:** Exact names required: `--bg, --surface, --surface-hover, --border, --text, --text-secondary, --accent, --accent-secondary, --positive, --negative, --warning` — NO other names (not --bg-primary, not --text-primary). **CRITICAL:** These exact property names are required for evaluation system compatibility. 43 2. **Utility Menu System (MANDATORY):** Complete `.viz-menu` element with `.viz-menu-toggle` button, `.viz-menu-dropdown` container, download PNG button (`onclick="downloadImage()"`), print button (`onclick="window.print()"`), and html-to-image CDN script (``). **EVALUATION CRITICAL:** Menu system is automatically checked and WILL CAUSE FAILURES if missing. 44 3. **Theme Classes (EVALUATION CRITICAL):** Must explicitly define BOTH `.theme-light` and `.theme-dark` classes in stylesheet with complete custom property definitions. **EXAMPLE REQUIRED:** 45 ```css 46 :root { /* base properties */ } 47 .theme-light { --bg: #ffffff; --surface: #f8f9fa; --text: #1a1a1a; /* etc */ } 48 .theme-dark { --bg: #0a0a0a; --surface: #1a1a1a; --text: #ffffff; /* etc */ } 49 ``` 50 **NEVER rely on just `:root` or `@media (prefers-color-scheme)` — evaluation system checks for class-based themes.** 51 4. **Semantic HTML:** `
` element, **MANDATORY: Multiple `
` elements for major content blocks** (header, metrics, charts, etc.), skip-to-content link. Each distinct content area must be wrapped in semantic `
` tags. 52 5. **Chart.js Requirements (EVALUATION CRITICAL):** MUST include `` before closing ``. **MANDATORY:** IMMEDIATELY after Chart.js script, add `` (prevents animation glitches and is automatically checked by evaluation system). **MANDATORY CHART VALIDATION:** Every chart function MUST start with `if (typeof Chart === 'undefined') { console.error('Chart.js not loaded'); return; }`. **CHART ACCESSIBILITY:** Every canvas element MUST have `role="img"` and descriptive `aria-label` attributes. **CRITICAL CHART CONFIG:** Set `maintainAspectRatio: false`, `responsive: true`, and `plugins: { tooltip: { enabled: true } }` for accessibility. **NEVER disable tooltips** - evaluation system checks for enabled tooltips. **CHART RELIABILITY SYSTEM:** Use dedicated ChartManager pattern for bulletproof integration: 53 ```javascript 54 var ChartManager = { 55 charts: new Map(), 56 safeInit: function(canvasId, config) { 57 if (typeof Chart === 'undefined') { 58 console.error('Chart.js library not loaded - check CDN inclusion'); 59 return null; 60 } 61 try { 62 if (this.charts.has(canvasId)) { 63 this.charts.get(canvasId).destroy(); 64 this.charts.delete(canvasId); 65 } 66 var ctx = document.getElementById(canvasId); 67 if (!ctx) { 68 console.error('Canvas element not found: ' + canvasId); 69 return null; 70 } 71 // Ensure no conflicting chart instances 72 if (ctx.chart) { 73 ctx.chart.destroy(); 74 delete ctx.chart; 75 } 76 // Set accessibility attributes 77 ctx.setAttribute('role', 'img'); 78 if (!ctx.getAttribute('aria-label')) { 79 ctx.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Chart visualization'); 80 } 81 // Initialize with enhanced error handling 82 var chart = new Chart(ctx, config); 83 this.charts.set(canvasId, chart); 84 return chart; 85 } catch (error) { 86 console.error('Chart initialization failed for ' + canvasId + ':', error); 87 return null; 88 } 89 }, 90 updateTheme: function() { 91 if (typeof Chart === 'undefined') return; 92 this.charts.forEach(function(chart, canvasId) { 93 try { 94 chart.update(); 95 } catch (error) { 96 console.error('Chart theme update failed for ' + canvasId + ':', error); 97 } 98 }); 99 }, 100 destroyAll: function() { 101 this.charts.forEach(function(chart) { 102 try { 103 chart.destroy(); 104 } catch (error) { 105 console.error('Chart destruction failed:', error); 106 } 107 }); 108 this.charts.clear(); 109 } 110 }; 111 ``` 112 Use `ChartManager.safeInit()` instead of raw `new Chart()`. **CRITICAL CHART CONFIG:** Set `maintainAspectRatio: false`, `responsive: true`, and `plugins: { tooltip: { enabled: true } }` for accessibility. **CHART CONTAINER DIMENSIONS:** Container must have explicit `height` >= 300px for charts to render properly. Use theme-aware colors with CSS custom properties, never static hex colors. **NEVER use import/export syntax with Chart.js CDN** — use standard var declarations only. 113 114 **CHART.JS TROUBLESHOOTING (CRITICAL):** If charts appear as blank white spaces: 115 - Verify Chart.js CDN is included before `` 116 - Verify `Chart.defaults.animation = false;` is immediately after CDN 117 - Verify chart initialization is in DOMContentLoaded event listener 118 - Verify no module import/export syntax anywhere in the file 119 - Verify ChartManager.safeInit() pattern is used correctly 120 - Verify canvas has `role="img"` and `aria-label` attributes 121 122 6. **Responsive Design:** Section spacing ≥48px, **CRITICAL: NO horizontal overflow at 375px viewport** (MANDATORY: add `@media (max-width: 375px) { body { overflow-x: hidden; } }` to prevent horizontal scroll), **MANDATORY FONT-SIZE HIERARCHY:** h1 ≥ 2.5rem, h2 ≥ 2rem, h3 ≥ 1.5rem, body = 1rem. **SLIDE DECK REQUIREMENTS:** Title slide h1 ≥ 3rem, content slide titles ≥ 2.5rem, clear visual distinction between heading levels. **SLIDE SECTION SPACING:** Major sections within slides must have ≥48px spacing (title-to-content, content-to-charts, charts-to-navigation). **Test all layouts at 375px width — dashboards especially prone to chart container overflow.** **CSS CONTAINER QUERIES:** For advanced responsiveness, use container-based queries: 123 ```css 124 .chart-container { container-type: inline-size; } 125 @container (max-width: 400px) { 126 .chart-legend { display: none; } 127 .chart-title { font-size: 1rem; } 128 } 129 ``` 130 This provides true component-level responsiveness beyond viewport media queries. 131 7. **Print & Accessibility:** `@media print` styles, `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` with disabled animations 132 8. **Entrance Animations (MANDATORY):** Must include entrance animations via `.animate` classes, `data-reveal` attributes, or CSS `@keyframes`. **EVALUATION CRITICAL:** Animation presence is automatically detected and required. 133 9. **JavaScript Functions:** `cycleTheme()`, `toggleMenu()`, top-level variables use `var` not `let`/`const` 134 135 **🔥 CRITICAL: Copy skeleton.md exactly → Replace "YOUR CONTENT HERE" with visualization content → Save file** 136 137 ## Core Principles 138 139 1. **Single-file HTML** — one `.html` file with inline CSS/JS. Opens in any browser, works offline, emails easily. 140 2. **Light theme optimized** — modern designs prioritize light mode quality. Dark theme available via toggle. 141 3. **Beautiful by default** — the first output should look professional with zero iteration. 142 4. **Content-first** — the visualization serves the message. Never sacrifice clarity for aesthetics. 143 5. **Responsive** — works on desktop, tablet, and mobile unless explicitly fixed-dimension (e.g., 16:9 slides). 144 6. **Visual restraint** — Professional designs avoid decorative elements that add noise. No floating gradient orbs, rainbow borders, or ornamental animations. 145 146 ## Philosophy 147 148 HTML is not a "website" — it's a visualization tool. Code is cheap. Everyone should feel empowered to visualize anything. This skill turns conversation context, URLs, articles, data, or raw ideas into something visual and digestible in seconds. 149 150 Users invoke this **mid-conversation** with Claude Code. Use the full conversation context — whatever they've been discussing, any links they've shared, any data they've pasted — as source material. When given a URL, crawl it and extract the content to visualize. 151 152 ## Output Rules 153 154 **MANDATORY FIRST STEP: Copy the complete skeleton from [references/skeleton.md](references/skeleton.md) — this includes all required elements (menu, theme system, CSS properties, semantic HTML, accessibility features). Never write HTML from scratch.** 155 156 - Write ONE `.html` file to `~/Downloads/` (or user-specified path) 157 - Filename: descriptive kebab-case, e.g., `q4-revenue-dashboard.html`, `team-roadmap-deck.html` 158 - Start with skeleton.md template, add your content to the `` section 159 - All custom styles in `

Now I'll build the poster HTML. This is an A1 portrait infographic poster with dark-mode dashboard aesthetic. I need to create a single self-contained HTML file that will be rendered to PNG. The poster needs:

1. Hero section with big callout stats (57, 206, 33×, $0.30→$10.00)
2. Intelligence ranking bar chart
3. Speed comparison bar chart  
4. Pricing landscape bar chart
5. Trade-off bubble/scatter chart (the visual centerpiece)
6. Methodology note

I'll write a comprehensive HTML file following the skill's skeleton, then render it to PNG using Python+Playwright.

import asyncio
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

async def render():
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        browser = await p.chromium.launch()
        page = await browser.new_page(viewport={"width": 1684, "height": 2384})
        await page.goto("file:///app/output/poster.html")
        await page.wait_for_timeout(2000)
        # Ensure all reveal animations are visible
        await page.evaluate("""
            document.querySelectorAll('.reveal').forEach(function(el) { el.classList.add('visible'); });
        """)
        await page.wait_for_timeout(500)
        await page.screenshot(path="/app/output/final_poster.png", full_page=True)
        await browser.close()
        print("Rendered /app/output/final_poster.png")

asyncio.run(render())

steps.message:
The poster has been successfully created and saved to `/app/output/final_poster.png`.

**Summary of what was built:**

- **Dimensions:** 1684 × 2384 pixels (A1 portrait at 72 DPI)
- **Style:** Dark-mode dashboard aesthetic with deep charcoal background, electric blue/teal/amber accents, and clean Inter typography
- **Sections included:**
  1. **Hero header** — Title, subtitle, and eyebrow referencing the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.0
  2. **Big callout stats** — 57 (highest intelligence), 206 tok/s (fastest speed), 33× price spread, and 10 benchmarks
  3. **Intelligence Rankings** — Horizontal bar chart with color-coded tiers
  4. **Output Speed** — Horizontal bar chart showing the counterintuitive insight that the fastest model isn't the smartest
  5. **Pricing Landscape** — Horizontal bar chart from $0.30 to $10.00
  6. **Trade-Off Bubble Chart** (visual centerpiece) — Intelligence vs. Speed with bubble size representing price, plus 4 insight cards highlighting best intelligence, best value, balanced pick, and premium tier
  7. **Methodology note** — Description of the 10 evaluations in the Index
  8. **Footer** — Source attribution

The output file is a single self-contained PNG image ready for use.
